findings.message: "Accessibility is a particular point of pride" is inverse framing that implies a low baseline is expected. It reads as surprise that the site scores well, equivalent to "better than expected given..." framing.
findings.context: Executive Summary: "Accessibility is a particular point of pride: we recorded zero distinct WCAG AA issue types across the audited set, meaning every visitor, regardless of ability or assistive technology, encounters the same content without barrier."

findings.message: The recommended action item "Review Priority 2-3 findings: metadata and schema improvements that compound over time" names only a domain category (metadata and schema) without a specific element, property, or action. No data anchor appears in this bullet — the specific Priority 2 finding is named in the preceding table row but this bullet itself adds no mechanism and could be copy-pasted unchanged into any audit report.
findings.context: Next Steps > Recommended Actions: "2. Review Priority 2-3 findings: metadata and schema improvements that compound over time"

findings.message: "Consider optional enhancements: optional patterns that give an early-mover opportunity in AI search" is a pure domain-framing sentence with no data anchor, no specific element, no named property, and no mechanism. It could appear verbatim in any web audit for any site.
findings.context: Next Steps > Recommended Actions: "3. Consider optional enhancements: optional patterns that give a early-mover opportunity in AI search"

findings.message: "puts the site in a different class" compound superlative construction. The phrase "machines can do considerably more than discover and parse the content" alongside "a position that gives the team a firm foundation" cumulatively reads as marketing copy rather than neutral consultant prose. Specifically, "considerably more" is an unsupported intensity claim — the audit data shows MX Readiness Level 5 but does not quantify the delta versus peers that would justify "considerably."
findings.context: Executive Summary: "With an MX Readiness Level of 5 (Purchase-confident) and MX governance markers present across the audited set, machines can do considerably more than discover and parse the content; they can read structured signals that support purchase-stage decisions."

findings.message: "ahead of most comparable properties" is an implied uniqueness / superlative claim. The benchmark medians in the scorecard (e.g. Discovery Readiness median 25, Structured Data Quality median 57) do support a lead, but the phrase "most comparable properties" is broader than the curated audit dataset citation warrants, and "well ahead" adds intensity the data can support only for specific dimensions. Flag as exaggeration for the cumulative effect.
findings.context: What's Working Well: "structured data quality that places the work well ahead of most comparable properties"

findings.message: "The full pattern is around 100 lines in any of these runtimes" is an effort/size estimate introduced in the narrative that does not appear in the audit facts block and cannot be derived from audit data. It is a fabricated specificity: a precise number inserted to add credibility to a recommendation that has no supporting measurement in this audit.
findings.context: AI Attribution section, edge-capture recommendation: "The shape is the same in each: a User-Agent classifier, a surface classifier, a small insert, and a non-blocking write that does not add latency to the user response. The full pattern is around 100 lines in any of these runtimes and backfills data from deploy day forward."

findings.message: "Set up custom regex channel groups in GA4... Takes about 30 minutes." is an effort estimate that does not appear in the audit data and cannot be derived from it. Effort estimates of this kind are fabricated specificity.
findings.context: AI Attribution > The 6-step playbook, step 1: "Match source/medium against `chat.openai.com`, `chatgpt.com`, `perplexity.ai`, `gemini.google.com`, `copilot.microsoft.com`, `claude.ai`. Takes about 30 minutes."

findings.message: "Enforcement penalties vary by jurisdiction and enterprise size: the EAA (Directive (EU) 2019/882) carries fines ranging from low four-figure to six-figure euro sums depending on severity" introduces specific penalty ranges ("low four-figure to six-figure euro sums") that do not appear in the audit facts and are not derivable from the crawl data. These are presented as precise facts but are unsourced narrative claims.
findings.context: PDF Documents section, Future work paragraph: "Enforcement penalties vary by jurisdiction and enterprise size: the EAA (Directive (EU) 2019/882) carries fines ranging from low four-figure to six-figure euro sums depending on severity, and Section 508 and ADA Title III carry litigation exposure in the US market."
